title: Taylor Swift Fires Up Academy Gala With Four Songs in Her First Band Performance Since the Eras Tour
description: Taylor Swift got some of the old gang back together for her first full-band performance since the Eras Tour, delivering a four-song set to a black-
body:
Taylor Swift got some of the old gang back together for her first full-band performance since the Eras Tour, delivering a four-song set to a black-tie audience Saturday night at the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala.

	Conan O’Brien introduced her by saying, “It’s an insane, unprecedented honor to introduce a cherished member of our little ‘Toy Story 5’ family. She’s John, Paul, George and Ringo all in one.”


	As an indicator of just how long she’s been off any kind of regular performance circuit, the gala-capping show included Swift’s first-ever live rendering of “The Fate of Ophelia,” the smash hit single she released just over a year ago, on Oct. 3, 2025. The song is expected to be a leading contender for record of the year and other categories at the 2027 Grammys, for which voters just received their first ballots.
	


	As expected, she also sang her contender for the 2027 Oscars, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the Pixar film “Toy Story 5.” It wasn’t her first live performance ever of that song — she did it at the Grammy Museum and at a private Ross House FYC showcase — but it was her first time singing it live with a full band, and not as part of a mash-up. Besides its Oscar eligibility, the song is also in contention at the Grammys, entered in the song of the year category as well as film soundtrack and country divisions.


	For the remaining two slots in her set, Swift dug farther back into the past, covering both her cynical and romantic bases, opening with “Blank Space” and ending with “Love Story.”
	



	

					Taylor Swift performs onstage during the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala in Partnership with Rolex at Academy Museum of Motion Pictures on October 17, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Stefanie Keenan/Oscars/Getty Images for Academy Museum Foundation)
									Getty Images for Academy Museum
	



	Wearing a Ralph Lauren gown for her performance, Swift invited the formally clad gathering to dance along with her set, saying, “Dancing is absolutely allowed. It’s not mandatory, but it’s more fun.”

	Her backing crew had some singers and players who would be familiar to Swifties, but also some differences in the lineup, which was stripped down in some regards and packed out in others, namely with a horn section. She was joined by two sax players — not a regular staple of her touring outfit — as well as four singers and a guitarist, bassist, keyboard player and drummer.

	Among the regular band members participating was Paul Sidoti, who wrote on Instagram, “Great to be playing music with my onstage partner of 19 years for the first time since The Eras Tour at a little party last night in Hollywood.”



	

					Taylor Swift performs onstage during the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala in Partnership with Rolex at Academy Museum of Motion Pictures on October 17, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Emma McIntyre/Oscars/Getty Images for Academy Museum Foundation)
									Getty Images for Academy Museum
	



	Swift posed for photos with attendees including “Toy Story 5” voice actors Joan Cusack and Conan O’Brian and celebs like Cara Delevingne, Sabrina Carpenter, Eli Roth, Charlize Theron, Colman Domingo, John Carpenter, Hannah Waddingham, Dakota and Elle Fanning.



	

					Sabrina Carpenter and Taylor Swift attend the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala in Partnership with Rolex at Academy Museum of Motion Pictures on October 17, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Stefanie Keenan/Oscars/Getty Images for Academy Museum Foundation)
									Getty Images for Academy Museum
	





	

					Taylor Swift performs onstage during the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala in Partnership with Rolex at Academy Museum of Motion Pictures on October 17, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Stefanie Keenan/Oscars/Getty Images for Academy Museum Foundation)
									Getty Images for Academy Museum
	







	

					Taylor Swift at the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala held at Academy Museum of Motion Pictures on October 17, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)
									Variety via Getty Images

title: Woodstock Film Festival Names Jessica Edwards as Executive Director
description: Jessica Edwards has been named the new executive director of the Woodstock Film Festival, the organization announced Sunday as the 27th annual fest
body:
Jessica Edwards has been named the new executive director of the Woodstock Film Festival, the organization announced Sunday as the 27th annual festival came to a close. Edwards will take over the role from Meira Blaustein, the festival’s co-founder.

	“I have had the pleasure of working with Jessica at the Woodstock Film Festival over the past few years, and I have nothing but the greatest respect for her,” said Blaustein. “As a filmmaker, a distribution consultant, and a former publicist, Jessica brings with her deep understanding, creative vision, and vast and strong contacts in the film industry. As a resident of the Hudson Valley, she knows and loves the region and its community. I am confident that she will not only retain the vision of the Woodstock Film Festival, which I have worked so long and hard to build and nurture, but will lead it towards an exciting new growth. I can’t wait to see what the next few years will bring. Welcome, Jessica!”
	

	Claude Dal Farra, who serves as president of the festival’s board, also welcomed Edwards appointment.


	“From our very first meeting with Jessica, it was clear to us that she was the natural person to succeed Meira and carry forward the extraordinary work Meira has done over more than 25 years,” she said. “Jessica understands what makes the Woodstock Film Festival special — its commitment to filmmakers, its independent spirit, and its deep connection to the Hudson Valley — while also bringing the experience, energy, and vision to lead it into its next chapter. On behalf of the Board, we are tremendously excited to welcome Jessica as our new Executive Director, and to work with her on the future of the Festival.”
	

	Edwards shared that this role is one she considers a “dream job.” “I’m honored to build on the founders’ legacy and help shape the festival’s future,” she said. “Woodstock’s history is shaped by its creativity, innovation, and independent spirit. I want to carry that spirit forward by bringing filmmakers and industry partners from around the world together with audiences here in the Hudson Valley. My vision for the festival is to create opportunities for people to meet, share ideas, and discover films together — connections that I hope will support filmmakers and inspire the next generation of cinema lovers.”

	The festival ran from Wednesday to Sunday, during which an Honorary Maverick Award was presented to Blaustein to recognize her leadership, more than 26 years of dedication to independent cinema and the legacy she has built.

	Festival winners included “Mouse” by Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson, “Rehearsals for a Revolution” by Pegah Ahangarani, “Washed Up” by Isabel Moncloa Daly and “They’re Here” by Laura Poitras & Rachel Lauren Mueller.

schema.headline: Woodstock Film Festival Names Jessica Edwards as Executive Director

title: CBS News Correspondent Jan Crawford Apologizes for Post on Abdul El-Sayed That Sparked Social-Media Ire
description: CBS News veteran Jan Crawford usually has the delicate task of covering the U.S. Supreme Court and the ways in which its decisions affect American
body:
CBS News veteran Jan Crawford usually has the delicate task of covering the U.S. Supreme Court and the ways in which its decisions affect American lives and policies. On Sunday, however, Crawford was the one being judged.

	Crawford, who joined CBS News in 2009, posted a note following a town hall meeting held  Saturday night in Michigan during which Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed parried with a young man named Tommy who asked him if he would “disavow the Muslim brotherhood.” The politician won approval from liberals on social media by discussing the right to religious freedom held by Americans under the U.S. Constitution.
	

	Crawford saw something different. In her post, she said El-Sayed spent just a “nanosecond” with a disavowal, the went into a “subsequent uninterrupted three-minute diatribe” that proved the questioner’s “exact point.” She called the exchange “the kind of spectacular self own most ppl only dream about triggering,” and offered a “congrats.”


	By Sunday afternoon, Crawford had deleted the post. “Earlier, I tweeted a video from an Abdul El-Sayed town hall,” she said. “I deleted that tweet because it was a violation of CBS News standards. I apologize.”

	CBS News declined to make executives available for comment.

	Crawford in recent years has walked on tricky terrain. She has become known for offering commentary, sometimes in public, sometimes in internal communications or meeting. Such behavior is typically frowned upon by most major news organizations, which want their reporters to be viewed as neutral chroniclers of the subjects and institutions to which they are assigned. Indeed, Disney’s ABC News opted not to renew the contract of longtime anchor and correspondent Terry Moran in June of 2025 after he called Trump administration official Stephen Miller a “world class hater” in a social media post.
	

	The Crawford controversy comes as CBS News has embraced more opinion under Bari Weiss, a digital entrepreneur who was named editor in chief of the Skydance operation in 2025. Weiss, who founded the provocative site The Free Press, has brought it with her to CBS News, and some CBS News personnel have written for the site. Ross Douthat, a former conservative opinion writer for The New York Times who has been named a correspondent at “60 Minutes,” recently debuted a column he intends to produce for the lively digital operation.

	Crawford is a journalist of long standing, working earlier in her career on the legal affairs beat for the Chicago Tribune after graduating from law school at the University of Chicago. She has also contributed analysis to what is now called the PBS NewsHour and worked for ABC News as well.

	In April, Weiss told Variety she was looking for people who could wear many hats at CBS News. ““The kind of talent that we are looking for are people who are amphibious. They are capable of, yes, reading off a teleprompter when necessary, but also doing man on the street interviews, speaking fluently in a casual podcast, writing in a clear and crisp way,” she said. “Candidly, what we are asking for of talent in 2026 is a lot. It’s special. And it’s not what has historically been typical. But there are people capable of doing it. We are just always going to be hungry for these people wherever they exist, whether they are inside CBS or if they are on the outside

	The attention to Crawford’s remarks comes as CBS News is trying to push forward after a series of surprising developments, including the overhaul by Weiss of “60 Minutes,” where ratings this season have been under constant scrutiny. The news division has recently seen some new momentum at “CBS Evening News,” where the overall audience watching anchor Tony Dokoupil has stayed above 4 million for two consecutive weeks, and is making notable tweaks to “CBS Mornings,” where Norah O’Donnell has joined the main on-air crew.

	But the news division is also grappling with its recent handling of reports about conflict in the Middle East. A “60 Minutes” report by correspondent Lesley Stahl from the region spurred arguments between her and Weiss, according to a person familiar with the matter. And Shayndi Raice, the CBS News foreign editor, in a meeting last week chastised some journalists working under her for resisting edits to their work made by senior staff and said pushback on direction — typical in many newsrooms as reporters on the ground vie with recommendations made by editors — could be viewed as insubordination. Raice’s comments came after she asked that a report by veteran Holly Williams be changed for broadcast on a later program, and were made available via an audio recording by the media newsletter Status and confirmed by two people familiar with the matter, one of whom noted that much of CBS News staff remains put off by the notion that questioning editorial direction could be seen as a firable offense.
	

	Crawford may have to decide if she wants to stay at CBS News and continue reporting on consequential affairs, or if she wants to pursue commentary, in which case she could follow the path of ABC News’ Moran. In April, the journalist launched his own website as well as a digital call-in show. Both allow him to speak his mind without having to worry about whether doing so will impugn the credibility of the legacy news organization for which he works.

schema.headline: CBS News Correspondent Jan Crawford Apologizes for Post on Abdul El-Sayed That Sparked Social-Media Ire

title: Box Office: ‘La Bola Negra’ Scores $277,500 From Four Theaters as Netflix Reports Grosses for First Time Ever
description:
In a major shift in the theatrical tides, Netflix has reported box office grosses for the first time ever. 

	The streamer’s awards hopeful “La Bol
body:
In a major shift in the theatrical tides, Netflix has reported box office grosses for the first time ever. 

	The streamer’s awards hopeful “La Bola Negra” scored $277,500 from just four theaters, averaging $69,375 per location. Those ticket sales are notable as the second-highest screen average ever for a non-English language film behind 2019’s “Parasite,” which opened to $393,216 from three theaters, averaging $131,072 per location. It’s also the highest-ever PSA — the key metric for arthouse releases — for a Spanish language film. By comparison, Neon’s multilingual legal thriller “Fjord,” another Oscar contender, debuted last weekend to $124,000 from four theaters, translating to $31,000 per location.
	

	Now the test is whether “La Bola Negra” can sustain momentum as Netflix slowly expands the movie’s footprint in the weeks to come. The streamer plans to keep the film in theaters for 45 days, a traditional window in post-pandemic times and the company’s longest theatrical rollout to date, before its Netflix release on Dec. 2. Directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, known as Los Javis, “La Bola Negra” is a generation-spanning queer epic that chronicles the interconnected story of three men. After the drama was embraced at Cannes Film Festival with a 16-minute standing ovation, Netflix acquired the movie for around $5 million. “La Bola Negra” tied for the Cannes best director prize and won Toronto Film Festival’s People’s Choice Award, which has historically been a reliable indicator of Academy Awards attention.


	Netflix has long been viewed as a major big-screen adversary, probably because the company’s co-CEO Ted Sarandos has frequently dismissed movie theaters as an “outmoded idea.” And while the streamer has been warming to theaters beyond just Oscar-qualifying runs, with token releases for 2022’s “Glass Onion: A Knives Out Story” and last year’s”Kpop Demon Hunters” re-release and the “Stranger Things” series finale, Netflix has never disclosed how much those movies made in cinemas.
	

	In the past, Netflix has viewed multiplexes, not as a financial strategy, but rather as a marketing stunt to drive interest pack to the platform. But there are other benefits to box office reporting for Netflix, which has never won the coveted best picture Oscar. Unlike streaming metrics, which can be twisted and touted in any which way, box office dollars are uniformly reported — meaning there’s no denying a hit (or a miss). Netflix’s change in strategy comes as the streamer’s stock has been languishing. Last week, the company laid off 1,000 employees and replaced chief content officer Bela Bajaria with Disney veteran Peter Rice.

	Moving forward, Netflix plans to disclose grosses for upcoming releases such as David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” around Thanksgiving and Greta Gerwig’s “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew” and Taika Waititi’s animated “Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory” in 2027. Whether those buzzy projects achieve breakout status, Netflix’s new attention toward theatrical is a win for exhibitors, who are already celebrating the biggest post-COVID year at the box office.

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘La Bola Negra’ Scores $277,500 From Four Theaters as Netflix Reports Grosses for First Time Ever

title: Charli xcx Brings Out Chappell Roan for ‘Boom Clap’ at Los Angeles Concert
description: As anyone who’s seen her in concert knows, Charli xcx is usually laser-focused on her current material and rarely looks back for more than a couple
body:
As anyone who’s seen her in concert knows, Charli xcx is usually laser-focused on her current material and rarely looks back for more than a couple of songs.

	But she made an exception on Saturday night at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles, when she performed her 2014 breakthrough hit “Boom Clap” (for the first time since 2023 according to setlist.fm), at the special request of guest Chappell Roan, who joined her for the song.




	“Every night on tour, I play an old song. I asked a friend of mine if she would come and sing an old song of mine with me, and they said, ‘The only way I’m doing it is if it’s this song,’ so you have her to thank,” Charli said before Chappell joined her onstage for the song.
	

	She didn’t stop there: Later in the evening, PinkPantheress came out for her own song, “Stateside,” followed by the Dare for an extended version of “Guess,” complete with pairs of underwear shot into the audience by a cannon.

	Chappell will be headlining her own festival in Los Angeles next weekend, the two-day “Super Graphic Spectacular.” 

	The comparatively short 12-date North American arena tour in support of her latest album, “Music Fashion Film,” launched in Philadelphia on Sept. 11 and included two nights at both Brooklyn’s Barclays Center and Los Angeles’ Kia Forum — the second of which is tonight (Sunday), followed by dates in Glendale, Calif. before wrapping in Las Vegas.

	“Music, Fashion, Film” dropped on July 24 and includes the singles “Rock Music” and “SS26,” with Charli pivoting to a more guitar-based sound than the electro-dance beats of its blockbuster predecessor, “Brat.”

schema.headline: Charli xcx Brings Out Chappell Roan for ‘Boom Clap’ at Los Angeles Concert

title: Jaime Pressly Defends ‘Mom’ Co-Stars as ‘Beautifully Flawed’ After Creator Chuck Lorre Revealed His ‘Reluctance to Hire’ Anna Faris
description:
Jaime Pressly has joined former “Mom” co-star Anna Faris in responding to show co-creator Chuck Lorre’s professional criticism.

	In his recent mem
body:
Jaime Pressly has joined former “Mom” co-star Anna Faris in responding to show co-creator Chuck Lorre’s professional criticism.

	In his recent memoir “Sitcom,” Lorre wrote that he “was, in fact, right” to be hesitant to cast Faris as the lead character, Christy Plunkett. Pressly, who joined the CBS sitcom in its second season as recovering addict Jill Kendall, came to the defense of her “incredible cast of women” co-stars.
	

	“I was there for seven years, but there [were] eight seasons,” Pressly told E! News. “I came on in the second season, but I had seven wonderful years of working with an incredible crew and an incredible cast of women, who were, all of us, just as beautifully flawed as our characters on the show were.”


	“And I think I just really thoroughly enjoyed being able to go to work with girlfriends every day,” she added. “All of us of a certain age, it was nice. It was refreshing.”

	Faris left “Mom” in 2020 ahead of its final season. At the time, she said she wanted to open herself up to other opportunities.

	“I wasn’t sure Anna would be appropriate for this kind of material,” Lorre wrote in his book. “Then I thought about how badly I’d bungled my working relationship with Charlie Sheen.” Lorre and Sheen had a public feud toward the end of “Two and a Half Men,” which led to the actor being fired from the hit sitcom in 2011.

	“As the years went by, it became apparent that my initial reluctance to hire Anna was, in fact, correct,” Lorre added about Faris. “After six years, she left the show for mysterious reasons that were not mysterious to anyone on the show.”
	

	Faris addressed Lorre’s comments on Instagram on Oct. 15: “Of course it hurts. Chuck gave me a job I loved, and for seven years I never took a day of it for granted. I’m proud of what we made together, and nothing changes how grateful I am for those people and those years.”

	She continued, “I’ve been sober for a year and a half. I was on a show about recovery and then I lived it. Now I’m healthy, I’m working, and I’m happier than I’ve been in a long time.”

	After Faris left the show, Pressly starred as the main lead in the final season. “Mom” also starred Allison Janney, Mimi Kennedy, Beth Hall and Kristen Johnston.

schema.headline: Jaime Pressly Defends ‘Mom’ Co-Stars as ‘Beautifully Flawed’ After Creator Chuck Lorre Revealed His ‘Reluctance to Hire’ Anna Faris

title: Georgina Cates, ‘An Awfully Big Adventure’ and ‘2point4 Children’ Actress, Dies at 51
description: Georgina Cates, the British actress who appeared in films including “An Awfully Big Adventure” and the TV series “2point4 Children,” has died. She
body:
Georgina Cates, the British actress who appeared in films including “An Awfully Big Adventure” and the TV series “2point4 Children,” has died. She was 51.

	Cates’s death was announced by her daughter, Naiia, on Instagram in June, though it had not been reported until now.

	“My beautiful, free-spirited mom lived a hard life and still found ways to make herself and others laugh and smile <3 now she can rest easy,” Naiia wrote. “I will always see you in black and white photos, Virginia slims, baggy clothes, no bras, big sunglasses, doodling while talking, pleasers, and flip flops and everything in between. I love you, thank you for your creativity, curiosity and your bravery to always be true to yourself — no matter what.”
	

	Cates began her career on “2point4 Children” in 1991, in which she played the character of Jenny Porter. She went on to appear in TV shows including “Casualty,” “An Exchange of Fire,” “Chris Cross,” “Crimewatch File” and “The Bill” through the early 1990s before making her feature film debut in “Au Pair” in 1994, which followed a young Welsh woman as she leaves her quiet country for Germany in search of adventure.


	In 1995, she starred in “An Awfully Big Adventure” alongside Hugh Grant and Alan Rickman. She also appeared in 1998’s “Clay Pigeons” with Joaquin Phoenix, Vince Vaughn and Janaene Garofalo, in addition to “Jackass Presents: Bad Grandpa” and “Everlasting,” among other projects.

	Georgina Cates was born on Jan. 14, 1975 in Colchester, England, and moved to Los Angeles to pursue acting. From 1997 to 2005, Cates was married to Skeet Ulrich, whom she met at an Oscars party, and the couple had twins, Naiia and Jakob. On Naiia’s Instagram post, Ulrich commented “I love you more than words can say sweetheart ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️”
	

	Cates is survived by her daughter, Naiia, and son, Jakob.

schema.headline: Georgina Cates, ‘An Awfully Big Adventure’ and ‘2point4 Children’ Actress, Dies at 51

title: Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber Remember Presley Gerber as a ‘Sweet, Beautiful Soul’: ‘We Love You Forever’
description: Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber took to social media on Sunday to remember their son and brother Presley Gerber, who died in September
body:
Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber took to social media on Sunday to remember their son and brother Presley Gerber, who died in September at the age of 27.

	“We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother. We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years,” wrote the family in the tribute, posted to Crawford’s Instagram. “He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever. We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability. We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain. Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia 🪽” 
	

	Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died at a rehab facility, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records. “The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time,” a representative told TMZ. A cause of death was not immediately known.


	Presley Gerber followed in his mother’s footsteps and began his own modeling career at the age of 15, signing with IMG Models and featuring in a campaign for Calvin Klein, the Moschino runway and a Pepsi ad alongside his mother.

	Presley Gerber had been open about his struggles with mental health and addiction. In 2019, he was arrested and charged with a DUI in Beverly Hills, and sentenced to three years’ probation. In November 2024, he began a series on his Instagram called “Mental Health Mondays” to “spark real conversations about the stuff most people hide,” he wrote at the time. “It’s been incredible seeing how far that message has spread and how many people it’s helped.”
	

	Kaia Gerber recently opened up about witnessing her brother’s addiction, telling Vogue: “When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone.”

	She added that she was very proud of Presley and his willingness to share his struggles. “My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn’t share anything — and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, ‘I’m gonna be very human for everyone,’” she said. “There’s only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you’re ashamed of them.”

schema.headline: Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber Remember Presley Gerber as a ‘Sweet, Beautiful Soul’: ‘We Love You Forever’

title: Aran Murphy on Playing an Angry Young Man in ‘Youth’ and ‘War’ — and His Father Cillian’s Influence
description: Aran Murphy is having quite a month, as he co-stars on not one, but two HBO shows — “Youth” and “War” — and plays one of the leads of Taika Waititi
body:
Aran Murphy is having quite a month, as he co-stars on not one, but two HBO shows — “Youth” and “War” — and plays one of the leads of Taika Waititi’s dystopian film “Klara and the Sun,” set to be released on Oct. 23. But if you think you’ve seen the 19-year-old actor before, it could be because of his strong resemblance to his Oscar-winning father, Cillian Murphy. “I don’t even think we look that much alike, but people seem to think otherwise,” the younger Murphy tells Variety.
	

	In both “War” and “Youth,” Murphy plays a troubled teenager negotiating complex relationships with his parents as they navigate divorce. “Youth” follows Sharon Horgan as a rambunctious 50-year-old divorcée dipping back into the dating pool. As her son Rauri, Murphy plays a creepy, brooding university dropout whom audiences also can’t help sympathize with. After only a few days at school, he returns home because a rumor has been spread about him and a drunken hookup that suggests he may be a predator. Did Murphy decide for himself whether Rauri is to be believed about his innocence during the incident? “Yeah!” he says. “I mean, I’d like to think so. It’s up to the audience; I don’t decide that. But I want to back my character.”


	Murphy’s and Rauri’s life trajectories are very different, but their timelines aren’t, which helped him get into character. “Contextually, we both just left school and were 18 — it was really about making decisions and whether college is the right thing, that kind of entrance into adult life, so that was a nice thing to draw on to relate to him,” he says.
	

	He adds that Hogan’s strong scripts and professionalism helped Murphy find his footing on set.

	“She was so awesome and charismatic and open to ideas that it was easy to just work and create that bond over shooting,” Murphy says. “The words were already so good, we were able to springboard off that and find the chemistry on the day.”



	

	



	In “War,” Murphy has a raucous introduction in the Oct. 15 episode as Gabriel, who’s torn between his mother (Sienna Miller as Carla) and stepfather (Dominic West as Morgan) during their ugly, high-profile divorce. Caught between Carla, a past-her-prime actress, and Morgan, a billionaire social media entrepreneur, Gabriel finds himself in the crossfire, used as an asset to negotiate between them. Like Rauri in “Youth,” Murphy similarly credits his character’s duality and relatability to creator George Kay.

	“It was all in the script — his frustration with what’s going on and nowhere to put it,” Murphy says. “I’m sure it’s a pretty universal kind of thing: People just want to take their anger out in some way.”

	One manifestation of Gabriel’s anger is physical, meaning that Murphy needed to throw a punch while the character is drunk at a party after his friend makes a rude remark about his parents’ divorce.

	“I’d never had to do something like that — that was new,” Murphy says. “That was a bit nerve-racking, because you don’t want to accidentally punch someone in the face.”



	

	



	Acting professionally is all pretty new to Murphy. Despite growing up with artistic parents (his mother, Yvonne McGuinness, is an Irish visual artist), Murphy originally saw himself on the football field.

	“That faded pretty quickly,” Murphy says. “I did a play when I was 11, and that was a really big deal for me. That was kind of the thing that showed me I wanted to [perform] for real when I became of age.”

	Murphy, of course, grew up watching his father act. “Seeing my dad onscreen in dramatic situations as an 8-year-old was pretty full-on,” he says, mentioning Ken Loach war drama “The Wind That Shakes the Barley,” which won the Palme D’Or at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival. “I think I need to revisit it as a 19-year-old.”

	He’s seen most, but “definitely not all,” of his father’s filmography, and is “forever grateful” for informing his film education at a young age, and having insightful conversations with him about acting. But Cillian’s biggest role for Murphy has been as a supportive father, rather than a public figure or acting influence. “I think living with someone who’s in the public eye, the novelty of that wears off pretty quick,” Murphy says.
	

	Murphy was more starstruck by working with Waititi on “Klara and the Sun” starring Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams. Based on the novel by Kazuo Ishiguro, the film follows Ortega as a robot girl experiencing the grandeur of human life for the first time. Though the movie is coming out this month, it was shot in early 2024 when Murphy was 16.

	“It was incredibly surreal. One minute I was in school, and then the next I was flying out to New Zealand and shooting a Taika Waititi film at 16, so it was just absolutely nuts,” Murphy says. “[Ortega and Adams] are so great, just being in their presence and being able to learn so much. They’re also so kind and accommodating. It’s just a massive learning experience, and I’m really grateful for it.”

	Despite his pride in the project, he says he’s “not a fan” of AI, adding “I don’t think it’s a net positive for the industry.” For Murphy, this film is important for “opening those discussions” about AI and “talking about the importance of human life and especially friendship and love and human qualities.”

	With this momentum behind him, Murphy says he’s eager to keep learning: “I’m just auditioning and crossing my fingers. Basically, I’m just open to anything.”

schema.headline: Aran Murphy on Playing an Angry Young Man in ‘Youth’ and ‘War’ — and His Father Cillian’s Influence

title: Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything’ Stuns With $15 Million Debut, ‘Street Fighter’ Leads With $31 Million
description:
“You Can See Everything” accomplished a true box office feat, becoming the rare must-see documentary on the big screen.

	Director Nathan Fielder a
body:
“You Can See Everything” accomplished a true box office feat, becoming the rare must-see documentary on the big screen.

	Director Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s much-hyped look at Elizabeth Holmes has generated a massive $15 million from just 855 theaters. Those ticket sales were enough for second place behind another newcomer, Paramount’s video game adaptation “Street Fighter,” which opened to $30 million from 3,575 venues. Heading into the weekend, “You Can See Everything” was aiming for $7 million to $8 million, which would have been remarkable for a documentary, especially one that doesn’t involve music or capture a wildly popular concert. Not to mention, this one runs at nearly three hours and wasn’t on anyone’s radar until two months ago.
	

	After a surprise world premiere at Telluride Film Festival, “You Can See Everything” became a word-of-mouth sensation, bolstered by some of the best reviews of the year. A24, which produced the movie in secret over three years for roughly $7 million, reported more than 2,000 sold-out screenings as audiences rushed to theaters to avoid spoilers on the stranger-than-fiction story about the Theranos founder before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. People are clearly captivated by the drama surrounding Holmes, whose rise and spectacular fall from grace was depicted in the Hulu series “The Dropout,” starring Amanda Seyfried. But the turnout for “You Can See Everything” also speaks to the commercial appeal of Fielder, who has developed a flair for blending reality and fiction through works like HBO’s “The Rehearsal” and Comedy Central’s “Nathan For You.” Oppenheim, his co-director, recently helmed another A24 hit, the Robert Pattinson-led “Primetime,” which has earned nearly $50 million against a $15 million budget.
	

	Around 70% of opening weekend crowds were under 35 years old, and they liked what they saw onscreen. According to exit polls, 90% of ticket buyers would “definitely recommend” the film and 80% said it was “even better than expected.” Those reactions signal a long theatrical life for the movie, which is expanding nationwide in the weeks to come.

	“This is a giant weekend for the genre,” says analyst David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “Documentaries rarely receive a wide release — there’s only one every other year — and they average $3 million over their first three days.” 

	This year has been an exception with two major docs, the other being Amazon MGM’s “Melania,” a $40-million-budgeted glimpse at first lady Melania Trump. That film opened to $7.1 million from 1,778 theaters — at the time registering as the biggest opening for a non-music or concert doc in over a decade — and ended its run with $16.3 million. (“You Can See Everything” carries a budget in the single digits and will be much more profitable than “Melania.”)

	Among its opening weekend bona fides, “You Can See Everything” secured the largest debut for any film playing on under 1,000 screens since 2006’s “Borat,” which ignited to $26 million from 837 theaters (not adjusted for inflation). And it’s the biggest opening for a documentary in over 20 years, since 2004’s seminal “Fahrenheit 9/11,” which premiered to $24 million from 868 theaters (not adjusted for inflation). Ticket sales for “You Can See Everything” are notable, not just for a documentary, but any arthouse release these days. By comparison, A24’s box office winner “The Drama,” anchored by two of Hollywood’s biggest stars in Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, opened earlier this year to $14.3 million from 3,087 theaters.

	Meanwhile, “Street Fighter” collected another $20.1 million overseas for a decent global start of $51.1 million. Critics and audiences were lukewarm on the video game reboot, which landed a “B-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls and a 42% on Rotten Tomatoes. Directed by Kitao Sakurai and starring Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji, “Street Fighter” follows two estranged fighters who are recruited to enter a tournament that forces them to face off against each other.
	

	Legendary and video game developer Capcom co-financed “Street Fighter” for $82 million, with Paramount only on the hook for distribution. The long-gestating film was originally set at Sony as part of Legendary’s pact with the studio and moved to Paramount once the initial deal expired. It’s the third movie based on the Capcom video game series following 1994’s box office winner “Street Fighter,” starring Jean-Claude Van Damme, and 2009’s misfire “Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li.”

	“Whalefall” and “Sense and Sensibility,” two other newcomers, launched in fourth and fifth place, respectively. Disney and 20th Century’s “Whalefall,” a survival thriller starring Austin Abrams as a scuba diver swallowed by a sperm whale, missed expectations with $8 million from 3,065 locations. The movie also floundered at the international box office with $9.5 million from 51 territories for a global total of $17.5 million. Reception was mixed, with audiences bestowing a “B” grade on CinemaScore and critics’ reviews averaging a 71% on Rotten Tomatoes. “Whalefall” cost $60 million and requires substantial staying power, since theater owners keep about half of ticket sales.

	“Sense and Sensibility,” the latest remake of Jane Austen’s classic, opened to $7.2 million from 2,545 screens. The well-reviewed movie has earned $11 million internationally, bringing its worldwide tally to $18.5 million. Led by Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles, the Focus Features film carries a $25 million budget and doesn’t have as high a hurdle to get out of the red.

	Neither film was able to outperform Universal’s horror film “Other Mommy,” which claimed the No. 3 spot with $8.3 million in its second weekend. Despite a painful 70% decline from its debut, “Other Mommy” is already a hit with $44.8 million domestically and $78.7 million globally against a modest $18 million budget.

	Elsewhere at the box office, “Digger” plummeted to No. 16 with $920,000 from 1,170 theaters in its third weekend, a shocking 77% decline. So far, Tom Cruise’s environmental satire has limped to $17.2 million domestically and $42 million globally. Warner Bros. spent above $160 million to produce the film, which is now primed to lose $245 million theatrically. Ouch.

	Among specialty releases, Netflix’s generation-spanning drama “La Bola Negra” collected $277,500 from four theaters in Los Angeles and New York — averaging $69,375 per location. Those returns stand as the second-highest screen average ever for a non-English language film behind 2019’s “Parasite,” which captured $393,216 from three theaters — averaging $131,072 per location. For a more recent comparison, Neon’s multilingual legal thriller “Fjord” debuted last weekend to $124,000 from four theaters — translating to $31,000 per location.
	

	This weekend is notable because it’s the first time Netflix has ever reported box office grosses. The streamer plans to keep “La Bola Negra” in theaters for 45 days, a traditional window in post-pandemic times, before the film’s Netflix release on Dec. 2. Directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, known as Los Javis, “La Bola Negra” was embraced at Cannes Film Festival with a 16-minute standing ovation and won Toronto Film Festival’s People’s Choice Award, which has become an Oscar precursor. 

	Overall, this weekend amounted to $101.6 million across all films, up 45% from the same frame in 2025 when “The Black Phone 2” led with $27.3 million. Meanwhile the domestic box office has hit $8.2 billion, nearly 20% above last year and just 8.5% behind 2019, according to Rentrak.

	“This is yet another eclectic, interesting weekend, and that has been the hallmark of 2026,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian. “When you have movies as different as ‘Street Fighter,’ ‘You Can See Everything,’ ‘Sense and Sensibility,’ ‘Whalefall’ and ‘Other Mommy’ playing together, you’re giving very different audiences a reason to go out to the movie theater — and that’s what works.”

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything’ Stuns With $15 Million Debut, ‘Street Fighter’ Leads With $31 Million

title: 'Happy Days' Anson Williams Ordered to Pay Ex Tens of Thousands in Divorce Dispute
description:
'Happy Days' Anson Williams
                          Not-So-Happy Ending to Divorce Drama ...
body:
'Happy Days' Anson Williams
                          Not-So-Happy Ending to Divorce Drama ...
                          Judge Orders $40K to Ex
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 18, 2026
                            1:00 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            "Happy Days" star Anson Williams is facing some not-so-happy news in court ... a judge has ordered him to cough up more than $40K to his ex-wife over unpaid divorce obligations.
      
    
            According to court documents, obtained by TMZ, Anson must pay his ex, Jackie Williams, $40,181.04 ... plus another $7,500 directly to her attorney, bringing the total bill to nearly $48K.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            And he's got a deadline ... the judge ordered Anson to pay everything by 5 PM on November 2.
      

            The money covers several expenses the judge found Anson failed to pay, including nearly $18K in life insurance premiums, roughly $17K in unauthorized use of company funds, and another $2K in payments he made to himself.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The judge also ordered Anson to transfer 160,214 American Express rewards points to Jackie ... so she's getting more than just cash out of this deal.
      
    
            The docs say Anson didn't show up for the October 1 hearing or file a response to Jackie's claims.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, Jackie dragged Anson back to court in August, claiming he'd failed to make payments required under their divorce agreement. She also claimed he ignored her attempts to collect the money.
      
    
            The former couple divorced in 2020 after 30 years together ... but clearly, their financial drama didn't end with the marriage.

title: Ecuador Priest Dies After Massive Crucifix Falls on Him During Livestreamed Mass
description:
Ecuador Catholic Priest
                          Dies After Cross Falls on Him Mid-Livestream
body:
Ecuador Catholic Priest
                          Dies After Cross Falls on Him Mid-Livestream
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 18, 2026
                            8:20 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 18, 2026
                                10:07 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A Catholic priest in Ecuador has died after a massive crucifix came crashing down on him in the middle of a church service ... and the terrifying accident was captured on a livestream.
      
    
      
      Catholic priest Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was killed when a crucifix fell on him during a service in Ecuador. Congregants tried to help, but he died from his injuries. https://t.co/u2b4DaZPok
              @Breaking911
          
  
    
            Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was leading Mass at Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church in Guayaquil on Saturday, when roughly 27 minutes into the livestreamed service the large wooden cross mounted behind the altar suddenly came loose and fell onto him.
      
    
            The service was being broadcast live online, and footage captured the shocking moment the crucifix toppled forward ... striking the priest near the altar as he addressed worshippers.
      

            The sudden collapse brought the service to an abrupt halt, with people inside the church reacting to the horrifying scene and rushing to help.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed Sánchez Molinari's death Sunday in a statement to Instagram, mourning the loss of the parish priest and offering condolences to his loved ones and fellow members of the religious community.
      
    
            Sánchez Molinari served as pastor of the church and was a member of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer, a Catholic religious order.
      
    
            It's unclear what caused the heavy crucifix to detach from the wall. Church officials have not publicly provided an explanation for the collapse.
